messages:
Alice M.: heads-up — customer AcmeApp says embeddings dims differ between deployments. Hosted /v1/embeddings returns vectors length 1024, but their Private instance returns 768. They claim nothing changed on their end. Can we triage?
Ben J.: ugh. do we know model + variant? hosted might be routing to a quantized variant. any request payloads?
Alice M.: sent sample request: `POST /v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-large input='[("foo")]'` — hosted response first vector length 1024. Private cluster response (they attached logs) shows model_id `redwood-embed-large-quant` and vector len 768.
Carol S.: hmm that sounds like an architecture mismatch not just quantization. quant usually preserves dim. maybe they fell back to a smaller model family? check model catalog and routing policy.
Alice M.: they said Dedicated also sometimes returns 768 depending on traffic. intermittent. runs fine in their dev on a pinned version.
Ben J.: intermittent across hosted/dedicated/private suggests routing or model alias resolution issue. possible scenario: alias `redwood-embed-large` maps to different underlying evrsions in different envs or there is model-surgery during on-prem sync.
InfraBot: deploy-note: 1768809000 alias-sync job completed on private cluster, changed alias mappings for `redwood-embed-large` -> `redwood-embed-large-v2-quant`.
Carol S.: ok InfraBot confirms alias sync. can we get the model specs for v2-quant? what’s output dim?
Ben J.: checking model metadata: `redwood-embed-large-v2-quant` -> embedding_dim=768 (reduced to save memory). `redwood-embed-large-v1` -> embedding_dim=1024. So alias change explains it.
Alice M.: customer says they didn't opt into reduced-dim model. they rely on stable vector dims for downstream index. this is a high-severity break for them. need rollback or migration path.
Carol S.: action: (1) revert alias on Private/Dedicated to v1 for AcmeApp tenant; (2) add tenant-scoped alias pinning to prevent global alias sync overwriting; (3) notify billing/CS team.
Ben J.: quick mitigation: if we can't revert immediately, we can serve v1 by forcing `model: "redwood-embed-large@v1"` in routing for tenant. however customer is using open `model: redwood-embed-large` alias.
Alice M.: customer wants a full repro and timeline for root cause. They also had charge spikes reported — could be caused by repeated retries as clients re-infer while dims mismatch triggers vector validation errors downstream.
Carol S.: log snippet from customer's dedicated instance: ```ERROR: embedding dim mismatch: expected 1024 got 768 for request_id=abc123; upstream returned model redwood-embed-large-v2-quant```
Ben J.: ok engineering notes: alias-sync job pushed to private clusters as part of config-rollout to keep catalogs consistent. there was a change in the sync config to map aliases by name without checking tenant pins. bug introduced in 1768808000 deployment.
Alice M.: can we get a timeboxed rollback? customer needs immediate fix.
InfraBot: rollback of alias-sync mapping for private cluster queued — estimated 15m. will mark in release logs.
Ops Bot: created incident INC-2026-045 and linked ticket #4567 for AcmeApp. escalation to enterprise support sent.
Carol S.: also confirm client's SDKs — some SDK versions auto-upgrade model aliases in requests. check if their requests explicitly pass model alias or let platform default. If SDKs request bare alias, they'll be affected.
Ben J.: tests to run before revert: run batch of sample inputs against private/dedicated pinned to v1 and v2-quant and compare dims, and run end-to-end downstream insert pipeline to ensure no silent failures. I'll run a quick smoke: `curl -X POST https://private.example.com/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":["test"]}'` and inspect output len.
Alice M.: customer asked about data loss risk and index compatibility. advise: vectors with different dims are incompatible; we must avoid silently mixing them. set immediate guardrails to block writes where dims != tenant expected dim.
Carol S.: good call. I'll file a config change to enable per-tenant dim validation and a soft-failure mode that returns explicit 4xx with error code `embedding_dim_mismatch` + helpful message.
Ben J.: also check batching config and mixed-deploy batching: if batching pools mix requests across model variants due to alias misrouting, that could create inconsistent outputs. ensure batching key includes resolved model id not just alias.
Alice M.: noted. customer also reported auth 401s earlier in thread — might be unrelated but worth verifying.
InfraBot: auth service logs: no failed provisioning for AcmeApp during alias change window. 401s were client-side token cache expiry; separate issue.
Carol S.: next steps summary: 1) revert alias on private/dedicated for AcmeApp (Infra 15m), 2) enable tenant pinning and dim validation, 3) run smoke test and share reproducible curl commands, 4) send CS note + rollback ETA.
Alice M.: thanks team. I'll update AcmeApp with ETA and mitigation (use explicit model spec or wait for revert). tagging @support-leads :thumbsup:
Ben J.: after revert we should add a regression test in catalog-sync pipeline that catches alias->model dim changes (alert if dims change for the same alias).
Carol S.: agree. I'll add a test ticket.
Alice M.: closing loop: customer confirmed they can pause ingestion until we revert. I'll post follow-up when Infra confirms rollback complete. :pray:
